scope: Proposition 5.1 of the manuscript “Ultraflat real Littlewood polynomials” (preprints/Ultraflat-real-Littlewood-polynomials-October-5-2026/ultraflat-real-littlewood-polynomials.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 076 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 89e4fd2beb7f4dab), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are absolute constants C > 0 and δ0 > 0 with the following property. For every 0 < δ < δ0, there are N0(δ) and Kδ < ∞ such that, for every integer N ≥ N0(δ), there is a continuous function BN : T → C satisfying BN (−t) = BN (t), 1 ≤ |BN (t)| ≤ 1 + Cδ (t ∈ T), (5.1) √ N | b BN (k)| ≤ 1 + C √ δ (0 ≤ k < N), (5.2) X k<0 or k≥N | b BN (k)| ≤ KδN−1 . (5.3) Its Fourier coefficients are real, and its Fourier series converges absolutely and represents BN .
